heading: Da Xue 大學 · The Great Learning (Legge 1893) · Da Xue 1 · Classic text (經) part 1 … Cultivating the person depends on rectifying the mind

items.text: Rest in filial piety toward your parents: honor, obey and care for them.
items.quote: As a son, he rested in filial piety.

items.text: Rest in kindness toward your children: treat them with gentleness and care.
items.quote: As a father, he rested in kindness.

heading: Da Xue 大學 · The Great Learning (Legge 1893) · Da Xue 14 · Commentary 10 (傳十) · Making the kingdom tranquil, part 3 … Making the kingdom tranquil, part 5

items.text: Make producers many and consumers few; be active in producing and sparing in spending.
items.quote: Let the producers be many and the consumers few. Let there be activity in the production, and economy in the expenditure.

items.text: Do not make revenue your chief business; seek righteousness as the family's prosperity.
items.quote: In a state, pecuniary gain is not to be considered to be prosperity, but its prosperity will be found in righteousness.

items.text: Do not keep a steward to lay imposts on the people; it is better to suffer loss than to oppress.
items.quote: the house which possesses a hundred chariots should not keep a minister to look out for imposts that he may lay them on the people.

items.text: Raise the worthy to office quickly; to delay is disrespectful.
items.quote: To see men of worth and not be able to raise them to office; to raise them to office, but not to do so quickly: this is disrespectful.

items.text: Remove bad men far away; to fail to remove them is weakness.
items.quote: To see bad men and not be able to remove them; to remove them, but not to do so to a distance: this is weakness.

items.text: Love what those under you love and hate what they hate; do not outrage natural feeling.
items.quote: To love those whom men hate, and to hate those whom men love; this is to outrage the natural feeling of men.

items.text: Pursue the great course with entire self-devotion and sincerity; pride and extravagance will make you fail.
items.quote: He must show entire self-devotion and sincerity to attain it, and by pride and extravagance he will fail of it.

items.text: Use wealth to make yourself distinguished, not to amass it at the expense of your life.
items.quote: The virtuous ruler, by means of his wealth, makes himself more distinguished. The vicious ruler accumulates wealth, at the expense of his life.

items.text: Do not let a mean man influence household administration; if you do, calamities will befall it.
items.quote: When he who presides over a state or a family makes his revenues his chief business, he must be under the influence of some small, mean man.

heading: Da Xue 大學 · The Great Learning (Legge 1893) · Da Xue 10 · Commentary 8 (傳八) · Regulating the family depends on cultivating the person … Making the kingdom tranquil, part 2

items.text: Cultivate your own person before you try to order your household.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: If the person be not cultivated, a man cannot regulate his family.

items.text: Do not let love blind you to your child's faults; know his bad qualities as well as his good.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: A man does not know the wickedness of his son.

items.text: Be as anxious for your infant as a mother, and learn to meet its wants.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: Act as if you were watching over an infant.

items.text: Treasure the affection you owe your parent above wealth or rank.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: What he considers precious is the affection due to his parent.

items.text: Treat the aged as the aged ought to be treated.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: When the sovereign behaves to his aged, as the aged should be behaved to, the people become filial.

items.text: Serve your elders with the submission owed to them.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: When the sovereign behaves to his elders, as the elders should be behaved to, the people learn brotherly submission.

items.text: Treat the young and helpless with compassion.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: When the sovereign treats compassionately the young and helpless, the people do the same.

items.text: Do not treat those under you in ways you would hate from those over you.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: What a man dislikes in his superiors, let him not display in the treatment of his inferiors.

items.text: Do not serve those over you in ways you would hate from those under you.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: What he dislikes in inferiors, let him not display in the service of his superiors.

items.text: Do nothing to your equals that you would hate to have done to you.
items.citation: The Great Learning, Da Xue 10, Commentary 8
items.quote: What he hates in those who are before him, let him not therewith precede those who are behind him.
